IPTW estimator (inverse-probability-of-treatment weights)

Source: R/methods.R
iptw.Rd

Linear-weighted Hajek estimator using the cluster-level IPTW identification weights of Leung (2025) (Proposition 3.9(iv)). Same outputs and variance rule as mrn: \(\hat\Sigma_1\) (Theorem 5.4) under Bernoulli randomization and the bias-corrected \(\hat\Sigma_3\) (Theorem 5.11(ii)) under complete randomization.

Usage

iptw(
  A,
  C,
  Y,
  W_C,
  W_Y,
  dist1 = "binom",
  params1 = list(prob = 0.5),
  dist0 = "binom",
  params0 = list(prob = 0),
  distC = "binom",
  paramsC = list(prob = 0.7),
  unit_weights = NULL,
  design = NULL
)

Arguments

A

n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix of the interference network (with self-loops, as used throughout the project).

C

integer vector of length n_unit giving each unit's cluster id.

Y

numeric vector of observed outcomes (length n_unit).

W_C

0/1 vector of cluster-level treatments, indexed by cluster id.

W_Y

0/1 vector of individual-level treatments (length n_unit).

dist1, params1

within-cluster assignment law of the treated regime phi_1.

dist0, params0

within-cluster assignment law of the control regime phi_0.

distC, paramsC

cluster-level assignment law.

unit_weights

optional per-unit weights u_i = g_i / N_i (default: uniform 1 / n_unit).

design

optional override, "bernoulli" or "complete"; inferred from distC when NULL.

Value

See mrn.

Examples

## Same data-generating pipeline as in the mrn() example: geometric
## cluster network, two-stage Bernoulli treatment, interference outcomes.
set.seed(1)
n_per <- 6; K <- 10; n <- n_per * K
C <- rep(seq_len(K), each = n_per)
centers <- cbind(rep(1:5, 2), rep(1:2, each = 5)) * 4
loc <- centers[C, ] + matrix(runif(2 * n, -1, 1), n, 2)
A <- Matrix::Matrix(as.matrix(dist(loc)) <= 1.5, sparse = TRUE) * 1

W_C <- rbinom(K, 1, 0.7)
W_Y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2))
Y <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y) +
                 W_Y * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y)) + rnorm(n))

## IPTW keeps only units whose neighbouring clusters are all treated
## (for phi_1) or all control (for phi_0), reweighting by the inverse
## exposure probability.
fit <- iptw(A, C, Y, W_C, W_Y,
            params1 = list(prob = 0.5), params0 = list(prob = 0.2),
            distC = "binom", paramsC = list(prob = 0.7))
fit$variance_type
#> [1] "var_1 (Loewner-max, Bernoulli)"
fit$causal_effects
#>                       effect            key estimate   variance        se
#> 1    Overall CE^O(phi1,phi0)     CE_overall 7.923015 1.76868306 1.3299184
#> 2          Direct CE^D(phi1) CE_direct_phi1 4.366624 2.33906215 1.5293993
#> 3          Direct CE^D(phi0) CE_direct_phi0 2.251229 0.02132106 0.1460173
#> 4 Indirect CE^I(1;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w1 7.496872 2.90504985 1.7044207
#> 5 Indirect CE^I(0;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w0 5.381477 0.29326263 0.5415373
#> 6      Total CE^T(phi1,phi0)       CE_total 9.748101 2.92637091 1.7106639
#>   well_defined
#> 1         TRUE
#> 2         TRUE
#> 3         TRUE
#> 4         TRUE
#> 5         TRUE
#> 6         TRUE
